info.title: PAIMOS API
info.description:
PAIMOS — Professional & Personal AI Project OS.

This is the **public, stable scriptable contract** for PAIMOS — the canonical resource surface used by the SPA, the paimos CLI, and custom integrations: auth, users, projects, issues, comments, time entries, attachments, documents, incidents, knowledge, and GDPR ops. It is intentionally a curated subset. Internal one-off admin tooling (CSV/Jira/mite imports, dev test reports, branding writes, SSO/TOTP management, AI operations, portal internals) is deliberately omitted and is NOT part of the stability contract — those endpoints exist but may change without notice. Authentication is either a session cookie (browser) or a `paimos_*` bearer API key (machine-to-machine). Coverage policy & contribution rule: PAI-294.

NotFound.description: Resource not found, or hidden from caller for privacy

PermissionsEpoch.description: PAI-320 per-user permissions epoch. The auth middleware sets it on every authenticated response, for session-cookie and `paimos_*` API-key callers alike, so it is always present on a success. The value is the canonical base-10 rendering of a non-negative int64 counter: no sign, no leading zeros, no surrounding whitespace. Clients compare it verbatim against the last value they saw and re-fetch `/auth/me` on any change, so a non-canonical rendering would silently invalidate that comparison. The pattern is exact on both ends: the counter is a signed int64 column rendered by `strconv.FormatInt`, so 9223372036854775807 is the largest value that can ever appear. The 19-digit alternatives encode that ceiling — one branch per prefix of the maximum whose next digit is lowered, plus the maximum itself — because JSON Schema has no numeric bound for a string-typed header.

SessionExpiresAt.description: PAI-322 session expiry. Present only when the request authenticated with a session cookie; absent for `paimos_*` API-key callers, so clients must treat it as optional. The value is the session's current expiry in UTC as an RFC 3339 date-time.

get.summary: Read bounded runtime layer health
get.description: Current nonimpersonated browser session with canonical Agent Mode project view access, including normal internal viewers. Reporter owner is reauthorized transactionally before any record enters the response. Latest runtime generation per machine, at most 32 visible records; no totals, offsets or unauthorized counts. Four closed layers per runtime. Missing evidence is unknown/not_reported; reports older than 60 seconds are stale; expired runtimes and their layers are offline. State and reason retain the last observed report and are not current healthy evidence unless status is fresh. No private proofs, credentials, paths, prompts or target references.

post.summary: POST consumer /streams
post.description: Exact API-key super-admin reporter with agent-controls:runner scope and private runtime proof. Consumer operations also require private consumer proof; claim/execute/complete require a unique exact attempt nonce. Headers are canonical unpadded base64url 32-byte proofs. Request limit 4096 bytes; duplicate and unknown fields refused. Claim returns NO payload. Execute commits executing before returning one transient payload; repeats never return payload. Lost response or ambiguous handoff is outcome_unknown and never re-leased. Expired unexecuted claims release safely. Stream fencing remains after expiry, preventing old binaries from claiming, requeueing or acknowledging owned work. Legacy leased work must drain first. Canonical FIFO deliveries, batches and cursors are preserved. Exact original completion retries retain original cursor after safe replacement. Runtime health is typed, bounded and coalesced into the existing attention ledger. No vendor exactly-once guarantee.

get.summary: GET lifecycle /runtimes
get.description: Non-impersonated super-admin browser session; CSRF required for mutations. Reauthorized transactionally. Unknown, foreign, revoked and wrong-provenance resources share lifecycle_unavailable. No totals or pagination counts. Responses never contain credentials, local paths, raw prompts or private target references. Max request body 8192 bytes; unknown and duplicate fields rejected. Runtime advertisements immutable; 120-second lease, refresh before expiry; never revive expired generation. Runtime registration reflects existing authenticated reporter Host->MachineID trust, not hardware attestation. At most 32 live runtimes and 32 live intents per project; durable replay records cap at 1024 runtimes/10000 intents. One claimed/executing intent per runtime. Expiry is materialized on authorized status/events/claim access. An executing state is permission/evidence to begin; it never certifies process completion. Claim retries return original claimed/executing work; crash recovery must not respawn unknown work. Browser status/history/cancel are restricted to creating user; execution also requires the exact originating session credential remain authorized. No changes to existing harness controls: pending=>requested, claimed=>claimed, applied=>completed, rejected=>failed. Steer delivery completion is delivery evidence only, not work completion.

post.summary: Send one authenticated human message to an exact owned worker generation
post.description: Non-impersonated internal browser session with transaction-current project editor authority. The selected managed non-stopping harness generation, revision, advertised simple/steer capability, current runtime reporter authority, and enabled primary target are checked atomically. The canonical ledger row is role human and from_address user:N; no agent attribution header is accepted or required. Exact replays return the original receipt after authorization even if the generation later stops; a changed tuple conflicts. Delivery snapshots only the selected target and never implicitly retargets a fallback. Text is valid UTF-8 up to 8192 bytes, preserves internal newlines, and rejects control or credential-like content without echoing it.

201.description: Canonical human message and delivery created, or exact replay returned

403.description: Uniform unavailable authority, generation, capability, runtime, or target

409.description: Stale selected revision or changed idempotent tuple

post.summary: Atomic revisioned owned control or retirement
post.description: Non-impersonated internal browser session with transaction-current project editor authority. stop and interrupt retain their existing control semantics. retire-after-work binds the human, project, revision, runtime generation and session generation in one durable idempotent request, fences new admission, and remains pending until accepted work settles and owned stop plus exact stopped-generation evidence exist. Browser clients never call the worker-lease drain endpoint.

403.description: Uniform unavailable authority, generation or capability

409.description: Stale review, changed idempotent tuple, assignment or competing control

get.summary: Get durable finish-then-remove evidence

get.summary: Authorized immutable assignment history
get.description: Non-impersonated internal browser session; transactional project editor for controls, viewer for history. Unknown/foreign/revoked/capability-denied is 403 harness_browser_unavailable; stale revision 409 harness_browser_conflict; malformed 400 harness_browser_invalid. No totals/private refs. Legacy routes unchanged. Revision checked before replay; pending same-kind control coalesces. History next is last returned revision. Body max1024 bytes; unknown/duplicate fields rejected.

get.summary: Issue current opaque Flow host context for an opted-in project
get.description: Project-viewer read. Returns host-issued local_host Flow identity and current baseline mapping for an INSPR-opted-in project. Ordinary authenticated sessions are local_host principals. Context is display data, not a credential. Missing, revoked, opted-out, or unauthorized projects fail closed. No raw session, token, email, role arrays, or invented organization. Imported Aithema approval is untrusted until current human review.

404.description: Unknown project, no view, or Flow not enabled.

post.summary: Revalidate a Flow intent against current host authority
post.description: Project-viewer revalidation. Consequential Review/Start intents reissue current context and refuse stale, wrong-project, expired, impersonated, or agent start authority. This route never starts a baseline batch, never introduces generic action dispatch, and routes humans to existing /projects/{id}?tab=overview baseline controls. CSRF required for browser sessions.

200.description: Intent revalidated and routed. executed is always false.

403.description: Agent or impersonated start authority refused.

404.description: Unknown project, no view, or Flow not enabled.

post.summary: Record typed implementation and scoped QA on a baseline batch
post.description: Project-editor mutation. Browser callers use a live non-impersonated session cookie plus CSRF. Automatic batches may instead use a live bearer API key whose owner is the start confirmer, with agent-controls:write, matching expected_runtime_generation and the stored worker account (expected_account_key omitted only for a validated class-only scope). Manual and assisted receipts require the human session; API keys are refused. Exact same-body replay returns 200 only when the payload and live authority still match; a changed payload on the same idempotency key is 409. Unknown and duplicate JSON fields are rejected before any StartStageRetry. Body max 65536 bytes. This route never exposes generic ReportStage, never PATCHes /runs, never starts deployment, and never mints handoff secrets. Authenticated reported evidence, not cryptographic proof a test ran.

200.description: Built receipt recorded, or exact authorized replay of the same payload.

400.description: Malformed, unknown-field, or semantically invalid receipt.

403.description: Authenticated but not the current editor, wrong automatic worker binding, or API key on a manual/assisted batch.

409.description: Conflict, stale CAS, cancelled/paused batch, or non-matching replay.

post.description: Live non-impersonated human session with project edit. CSRF required. Attribution is the recording human; this is attestation, not verified sender identity. Remote HTML content is rejected.

get.summary: Export acceptance evidence
get.description: Live human session with project view. format=json|eml|html. Evidence stays authorization-checked. HTML is escaped and does not load remote content.

post.summary: Bind an exact deployment target to this release
post.description: Live non-impersonated human session with project edit. CSRF required. Existence of a Pharos owner environment or a sole project environment is not selection. The bound identity includes registration or environment row id, delivery/attempt generation, and created_at so same-name retargeting, revocation, and generation changes invalidate standing policy. No fallback across namespaces.

200.description: Updated acceptance projection with the bound target identity.

get.summary: List customer-operated standing policies
get.description: Live human session with project view. Standing policy is never inferred from cooperation notes.

post.summary: Approve a customer-operated standing policy
post.description: Live non-impersonated human session with project edit. CSRF required. Customer-operated only. Does not authorize future email sends. target_ref is the provenance digest of an explicitly bound deployment target for this baseline. model_ref is the customer-operated arrangement. Names, artifact coordinates, and inferred sole environments are refused.

post.summary: Revoke a standing policy
post.description: Live non-impersonated human session with project edit. CSRF required.

post.summary: Apply a standing policy to the current actor's own party
post.description: Live non-impersonated human session with project view. Confirms only the current actor's listed party when the policy still matches. Does not send mail. Drift, expiry, revocation, unknown deployment target, or agency modes force fresh confirmation.

403.description: Policy does not cover this party or mode.
